results.question: According to Table 1, what is the release time, size in billions, and training hardware for PanGu-alpha?
results.answer: PanGu-alpha was released in Apr-2021, has size 13B* (or up to 200B), and was trained on 2048 Ascend 910 hardware. (Source: [Page 8, Table 1])

results.question: In Table 3, what are the collection names, categories, and number of examples for Alpaca and ShareGPT?
results.answer: Alpaca is in the Synthetic category with 52K examples (Mar-2023); ShareGPT is in the Chat category with 90K examples (Mar-2023). (Source: [Page 14, Table 3])

results.question: According to Table 5, what normalization method, number of layers (#L), and hidden dimension (d_model) are used by GPT-3 (175B)?
results.answer: GPT-3 (175B) uses PreLayerNorm, #L = 96 layers, and d_model = 12288. (Source: [Page 23, Table 5])

results.question: In Table 8, what is the optimizer, learning rate, and precision type configured for PaLM (540B)?
results.answer: PaLM (540B) uses the Adafactor optimizer, learning rate 1 x 10^-2, and BF16 precision. (Source: [Page 29, Table 8])

results.question: According to Table 9, how many A800 GPUs and tuning time are required for full parameter tuning of LLaMA (65B)?
results.answer: Full tuning of LLaMA (65B) requires 16 A800 GPUs with batch size 2, taking approximately 112 hours. (Source: [Page 33, Table 9])

results.question: According to Table 21, what is the memory footprint in GiB for LLaMA (13B) across 16-bit, 8-bit, and 4-bit quantizations?
results.answer: LLaMA (13B) requires 24.40 GiB in 16-bit, 12.53 GiB in 8-bit, and 7.34 GiB in 4-bit quantization. (Source: [Page 88, Table 21])

results.question: According to Figure 2, what are the four generations of language models from the perspective of task solving capacity?
results.answer: The four generations are: Statistical Language Models (SLM), Neural Language Models (NLM), Pre-trained Language Models (PLM), and Large Language Models (LLM). (Source: [Page 2, Figure 2])

results.question: According to Figure 7, what are the major stages in the typical data preprocessing pipeline for pre-training LLMs?
results.answer: The preprocessing pipeline includes Quality Filtering (language filtering, heuristic rules), De-duplication, Privacy Redaction (PII removal), and Tokenization. (Source: [Page 19, Figure 7])

results.question: In Figure 11, what three methods are illustrated for constructing instruction-formatted instances?
results.answer: The three methods illustrated are: formatting existing NLP datasets, collecting real human/user instructions (e.g. InstructGPT), and generating synthetic instructions using LLMs (e.g. Self-Instruct). (Source: [Page 31, Figure 11])

results.question: According to Figure 15, what is the evolutionary progression of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategies?
results.answer: It begins with basic CoT, progresses to enhanced CoT generation techniques (sampling-based and verification-based), and extends to non-linear structures such as trees (Tree of Thoughts) and graphs. (Source: [Page 53, Figure 15])

results.question: In Figure 16, what are the key components of prompt-based planning by LLMs for solving complex tasks?
results.answer: The framework consists of a Task Planner (plan generation), a Plan Executor, an Environment providing feedback, and Plan Refinement mechanisms. (Source: [Page 54, Figure 16])

results.question: In Figure 1(b), how did the daily average publication rate of arXiv papers containing large language model change before and after ChatGPT?
results.answer: The average number of published arXiv papers per day mentioning large language model increased sharply from 0.40 per day to 8.58 per day after the release of ChatGPT. (Source: [Page 2, Figure 1 & text])

results.question: According to Figure 3, how are models with publicly available checkpoints visually distinguished in the timeline?
results.answer: In Figure 3, models with publicly available checkpoints are highlighted with a distinct yellow background. (Source: [Page 9, Figure 3])

results.question: In Figure 5, what open-source LLM research family is tracked, and how do the authors support incremental updates of this chart?
results.answer: Figure 5 tracks the evolutionary graph of the LLaMA research family; authors share the source file and invite community pull requests on GitHub for incremental updates. (Source: [Page 12, Figure 5])

results.question: In Figure 8, what aspects of pre-training data scheduling are illustrated?
results.answer: Figure 8 illustrates data scheduling along two dimensions: adjusting the mixing ratios of diverse data sources during training, and curriculum learning from simple to complex data. (Source: [Page 20, Figure 8])

results.question: In Figure 10, what context sentence is used to illustrate the next-token probability distribution over vocabulary?
results.answer: The context sentence is I am sleepy. I start a pot of, used to display the descending probability distribution for subsequent tokens such as coffee. (Source: [Page 26, Figure 10])

results.question: According to Figure 17 and Section 7.1, what example is used to demonstrate intrinsic hallucination regarding Bob, Amy, and Cindy, and why is it contradictory?
results.answer: Given the context that Bob is married to Amy and Cindy is Bob daughter, the LLM hallucinates that Cindy is Amy daughter-in-law, directly contradicting the premise that Cindy is Amy daughter. (Source: [Page 59, Figure 17 & Section 7.1])

results.question: Comparing Table 1 and Section 3.3.1, when was LLaMA introduced by Meta, what sizes were released, and how does Figure 5 reflect its ecosystem?
results.answer: LLaMA was introduced in Feb-2023 with sizes 7B, 13B, 30B, and 65B (Table 1 & Section 3.3.1), sparking an extensive open-source fine-tuning and adaptation ecosystem visualized in Figure 5. (Source: [Page 8, Table 1, Section 3.3.1, Figure 5])

results.question: In Table 5, what position embedding method does BLOOM use, and how does Section 4.3 compare its length extrapolation properties to standard sinusoidal embeddings?
results.answer: BLOOM uses ALiBi (Table 5). Section 4.3 notes that ALiBi applies pre-defined static penalties on attention scores without trainable parameters, demonstrating superior length extrapolation compared to sinusoidal PE. (Source: [Page 23, Table 5 & Section 4.3])

results.question: According to Table 14 and Section 6.1, what are two benchmark datasets used for closed-book QA, and what core ability does this evaluate?
results.answer: Datasets such as Natural Questions and TriviaQA (Table 14) are used for Closed-Book QA, evaluating the model Knowledge Utilization and factual retrieval ability without external retrieval. (Source: [Page 57, Table 14 & Section 6.1])

results.question: How does the survey define emergent abilities in Large Language Models, and what are typical examples?
results.answer: Emergent abilities are abilities that are not present in smaller language models but emerge abruptly when the model size exceeds a certain critical threshold (e.g., in-context learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, multi-step math). (Source: [Page 6, Section 2.2.1])

results.question: What are the three criteria of human alignment (the 3H criteria) emphasized in the survey?
results.answer: The 3H criteria are: Helpful (assisting users effectively to solve tasks), Honest (providing accurate, truthful information without fabricating), and Harmless (avoiding hate speech, bias, or toxic content). (Source: [Page 36, Section 5.2.1])

results.question: What is the role of DeepSpeed ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer) in distributed training of LLMs?
results.answer: ZeRO eliminates memory redundancies in data-parallel training by partitioning optimizer states (ZeRO-1), gradients (ZeRO-2), and model parameters (ZeRO-3) across data-parallel processes. (Source: [Page 82, Section 4.3.2 / Section 8])

results.question: What is the Self-Instruct method and what was its original seed task requirement?
results.answer: Self-Instruct generates synthetic instruction tuning datasets iteratively using an LLM itself, starting from a small curated seed pool of only 175 human-written tasks. (Source: [Page 15, Section 4.1.2])
